title: Descent of open subfunctors along an fppf-local scheme presentation
statement: Let $S,U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $U$ over $S$, and let $F,G$ be sheaves of sets on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $h_X(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,X)$ for each $S$-scheme $X$. Let $\alpha:G\to F$ be a natural transformation injective on sections over every $S$-scheme, and let $q:h_U\to F$ be a natural transformation such that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $a\in F(T)$ there is an fppf covering $\{\varphi_i:T_i\to T\}$ and maps $a_i:T_i\to U$ with $q(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$. Suppose $W\subseteq U$ is an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] and there is an isomorphism $h_W\simeq h_U\times_{F,q,\alpha}G$ over $h_U$ [def-pc-fibre-product], whose projection to $h_U$ is the open inclusion. For any $T,a$ and any such covering and lifts, put $W_i=a_i^{-1}(W)$. Then the pullbacks of $W_i,W_j$ to $T_i\times_TT_j$ are equal, and there is a unique open subscheme $W_{T,a}\subseteq T$ with $\varphi_i^{-1}(W_{T,a})=W_i$ for every $i$. There is a natural isomorphism over $h_T$, $h_{W_{T,a}}\simeq h_T\times_{F,a,\alpha}G$. The open and this isomorphism are independent of the covering and lifts and commute with every scheme base change $Z\to T$; in particular $\alpha$ is representable by open immersions. No algebraic-space or representability assumption on $F,G$ or $q$ is made.

proof.text: Evaluate the assumed pullback isomorphism on E. Types.exists_of_isPullback and eW identify a section g of G(E) mapping to q(b) with a factorization of b:E→U through W. IsOpenImmersion.lift and its factorization equation identify such a factorization with range(b) contained in W. Applied to composites E→B→U, this is the same criterion for the inverse-image open b⁻¹W. Uniqueness of g follows from sectionwise injectivity.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), local representing property, applied to the given pullback isomorphism; Schemes Tags 01JY and 01HI

proof.text: On $B=T_i\times_TT_j$, write $b_i=a_i\mathrm{pr}_i$ and $b_j=a_j\mathrm{pr}_j$. Naturality and the lift equations give $q(b_i)=a|_B=q(b_j)$. Put $O_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(W_i)$ and $O_j=\mathrm{pr}_j^{-1}(W_j)$. The identity inclusion $O_i\to B$ factors through $O_i$, hence step 1 supplies a section of $G(O_i)$ mapping to $q(b_i)|_{O_i}=q(b_j)|_{O_i}$. Step 1 for $b_j$ implies that this inclusion factors through $O_j$, so $O_i\subseteq O_j$. Interchanging $i,j$ gives equality. Since both opens have the restricted structure sheaf, their open subschemes agree.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), equality of the two overlap opens; generalization using the given pullback square

proof.text: The given fppf family is fpqc by Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage (Stacks Tag 022C). This directly discharges the covering hypothesis of openSubscheme_existsUnique_of_fpqc, without a separate affine refinement.

Apply descent of compatible opens to the fpqc family from step 3 and the overlap equalities from step 2. It gives a unique open subscheme $V=W_{T,a}\subseteq T$ with $\varphi_i^{-1}(V)=W_i$ for every $i$. This applies to arbitrary covering families, including the empty covering of the empty scheme.

For f:E→T, pull back the chosen fppf covering to E using the precoverage base-change axiom. If range(f) is contained in V, its composites from the covering members factor through the chart inverse-image opens, so step 1 supplies sections of G there. Extend these sections along the generated covering sieve. Their images under alpha are restrictions of a(f); injectivity implies compatibility. The sheaf condition in G glues them, and separation in F identifies the image of the glued section with a(f). This is the private image_local and criterion_of_descent argument.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), paragraph proving the descended open defines a section of the subsheaf; here the sectionwise gluing is written out

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $g\in G(Z)$ satisfies $\alpha(g)=f^*a$. On the same fppf covering $Z_i\to Z$, step 1 applied to $g|_{Z_i}$ says that $r_i$ factors through $W_i$. Hence $f p_i$ has image in $V$. Joint surjectivity of this covering implies $f(Z)\subseteq V$: given $z\in Z$, take $z_i$ over $z$ and use $f(z)=f p_i(z_i)$. The open-factorization theorem gives a unique factorization $Z\to V\hookrightarrow T$. This proves both implications for every test scheme and every $f$.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), final paragraph proving the representing property; Schemes Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens)

proof.text: For every test E and f:E→T, steps 5 and 6 give existence of g with alpha(g)=a(f) exactly when range(f) is contained in V. Apply this to the inclusion j:V→T to get a section g on V; Yoneda makes it a natural transformation h_V→G. Together with h_V→h_T it is a pullback square: pointwise, open factorization proves existence, the mono j proves uniqueness, and alpha-injectivity identifies the second component. IsPullback.isoPullback gives the required isomorphism over h_T.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), conclusion that the descended open represents the fibre product

proof.text: Any isomorphism over h_T is unique because pullback.fst a alpha is mono. The pointwise criterion shows that for any other fppf family with lifts, phi_i⁻¹V equals ai_i⁻¹W, by testing their open inclusions; joint surjectivity gives uniqueness among all opens with those inverse images. For arbitrary b:Z→T, the criterion for (Z,b*a) is exactly the criterion for b⁻¹V, so testing both inclusions proves equality. Finally evaluate pullback.condition and the projection equations on each test map: equal composites into T give equal images in F of the G-components; injectivity gives equality in G. No nonempty-cover hypothesis is used.

lean.statement: theorem fppf_local_open_subfunctor_descent {S : Scheme.{u}} (U : Over S) (F G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (α : G.obj ⟶ F.obj) (hα : ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (α.app (op T))) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F.obj) (hq : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) q) (W : U.left.Opens) (eW : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (W.ι ≫ U.hom)) ≅ pullback q α) (heW : eW.hom ≫ pullback.fst q α = yoneda.map (Over.homMk W.ι)) : ∃ (V : ∀ (T : Over S), (yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) → T.left.Opens) (e : ∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj), yoneda.obj (Over.mk ((V T a).ι ≫ T.hom)) ≅ pullback a α), (∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj), (e T a).hom ≫ pullback.fst a α = yoneda.map (Over.homMk (V T a).ι)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) (e' : yoneda.obj (Over.mk ((V T a).ι ≫ T.hom)) ≅ pullback a α), e'.hom ≫ pullback.fst a α = yoneda.map (Over.homMk (V T a).ι) → e' = e T a) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) (I : Type v) (Ti : I → Over S) (φ : ∀ i, Ti i ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (Ti i).left) (fun i ↦ (φ i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left → ∀ ai : ∀ i, Ti i ⟶ U, (∀ i, yoneda.map (ai i) ≫ q = yoneda.map (φ i) ≫ a) → (∀ i j, pullback.fst (φ i).left (φ j).left ⁻¹ᵁ ((ai i).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) = pullback.snd (φ i).left (φ j).left ⁻¹ᵁ ((ai j).left ⁻¹ᵁ W)) ∧ (∀ i, (φ i).left ⁻¹ᵁ V T a = (ai i).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) ∧ (∀ O : T.left.Opens, (∀ i, (φ i).left ⁻¹ᵁ O = (ai i).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) → O = V T a)) ∧ (∀ (Z T : Over S) (b : Z ⟶ T) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj), V Z (yoneda.map b ≫ a) = b.left ⁻¹ᵁ V T a) ∧ (∀ (Z T : Over S) (b : Z ⟶ T) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) (E : Over S) (vZ : E ⟶ Over.mk ((V Z (yoneda.map b ≫ a)).ι ≫ Z.hom)) (vT : E ⟶ Over.mk ((V T a).ι ≫ T.hom)), vZ ≫ Over.homMk (V Z (yoneda.map b ≫ a)).ι ≫ b = vT ≫ Over.homMk (V T a).ι → (pullback.snd (yoneda.map b ≫ a) α).app (op E) ((e Z (yoneda.map b ≫ a)).hom.app (op E) vZ) = (pullback.snd a α).app (op E) ((e T a).hom.app (op E) vT))
